newsitem.title: USA: May 27-30 NYSE program trading averages 14.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: May 27-30 NYSE program trading averages 14.7 pct.

text.p: The New York Stock Exchange said Thursday that program trading accounted for an average 14.7 percent, or 70.8 million shares, of the average daily volume of 480.5 million shares during the week from May 27 through May 30.
In the previous week such trading accounted for 15.4 percent, or 67.5 million shares, of average daily volume of 438.3 million shares.
In all markets program trading averaged 107.8 million shares per day during the week beginning May 27.

Of the five member firms reporting the most program activity on the NYSE, the exchange said that BNP Securities, Natwest, Salomon Brothers and Interactive Brokers executed all or most of their program trading for customers. Morgan Stanley executed most of its program trades for its own account.

Program trades executed by firms for non-member customers totaled 68.7 percent during the week beginning May 27. Such trades executed for their own accounts amounted to 30.3 percent of program volume.
In the same week, 18.7 percent of program trading involved index arbitrage, while another 0.8 percent involved derivative product-related strategies.
Program trading encompasses trading strategies involving the sale of a basket of at least 15 securities with a value of $1 million or more.
